items.title: ETAMem: Decoupling and Aligning Heterogeneous Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents
items.summary_1line: Long-term memory enables Large Language Models (LLMs) to maintain coherent and personalized interactions across extended conversations. However, existing memory systems face two key challenges: (1) Information Entangl...
items.editor_note: Opens the current window with an architecture claim: mixed memory types get entangled, so store them separately and align them.

items.title: A State Change Is Local, Its Consequences Are Not: Dependency-Aware State Revision for Long-Term Agent Memory
items.summary_1line: Long-lived agents rely on persistent memory of users, tasks and decisions, and this memory must stay consistent with a world that keeps changing. When an upstream fact changes, however, memory systems can revise the c...
items.editor_note: Adds the consistency problem: revising one fact is not enough when other stored memories depend on it.

items.title: What Is This Memory Useful For? Measuring Task-Conditioned Utility in Long-Term Agent Memory
items.summary_1line: A stored experience may answer one future question and offer little help with another. We measure this task-conditioned utility rather than assigning each memory a single importance score. A task-blind writer stores a...
items.editor_note: Replaces a single importance score per memory with usefulness measured against the specific future task.

items.title: Twists and Turns: A Graph-Based Benchmark and Framework for Long-Term Memory in Exploration Tasks
items.summary_1line: Long-term problem-solving processes, such as scientific research and software development, proceed along an evolving trial-and-error trajectory toward a central goal. We term these \textit{exploration tasks}, which re...
items.editor_note: Extends memory evaluation from conversation to long trial-and-error trajectories, with a graph-based benchmark and framework.

items.title: MIGRO: A Decoupled and Portable Long-Term Memory System for Language Models
items.summary_1line: Language models evolve, but the observations, revisions, and context accumulated through user interactions should remain usable. Each new model must be able to retrieve past evidence, track revisions, and add new observations. We present MIGRO, a decoupled long-term memory system
items.editor_note: Treats memory as an asset that should outlive the model: retrieve past evidence, track revisions, and add observations after a model change.

items.title: We Are What We Remember: Mental-State-Driven Memory for Long-Term Character Dialogue
items.summary_1line: Shared history in human dialogue is not merely a repository of facts, but the foundation of evolving relationships and mutual understanding. However, mainstream conversational memory systems rely on passive semantic s...
items.editor_note: Shifts the goal from fact recall to relationship continuity in character dialogue, driven by modeled mental state.

editorial.tldr: This is a topical cluster of independent long-term-memory work, not one developing event; its August items argued that recall-only evals miss whether an agent uses what it retrieves. Since Oct 27 the focus has moved from recall to upkeep: separating entangled memory types, revising dependent facts, scoring memories per task, sealing provenance, and porting memory across models.
editorial.whats_new: A Nov 12 arXiv paper proposes mental-state-driven memory for long-term character dialogue, arguing that shared history is the basis of an evolving relationship rather than a repository of facts.
editorial.why_it_matters: Six of the seven items target what happens after a memory is written: revision when an upstream fact changes, per-task usefulness, provenance, and survival across a model swap. Those are the failure modes a recall benchmark does not exercise.
editorial.take_for_builders: Add a stale-dependency case to your memory evals: change one upstream fact, then check whether the agent still acts on stored conclusions that depended on it.

beats.headline: ETAMem separates heterogeneous memory types for conversational agents
beats.summary: The paper names information entanglement as a core problem in existing memory systems and proposes decoupling, then aligning, the different kinds of memory.

beats.headline: A changed fact leaves its downstream consequences stale
beats.summary: Dependency-aware state revision treats an update as more than a local edit: what was derived from the old fact has to be revised too.

beats.headline: Two papers measure memory by task, not by a single score
beats.summary: One scores how useful a stored experience is for a given future task; the other adds a graph-based benchmark for trial-and-error work such as research and software development.

beats.headline: Provenance containment and model-portable memory
beats.summary: MemSeal, a Show HN project, contains memory by provenance; MIGRO decouples the memory system from the model so accumulated observations and revisions survive a model change.

beats.headline: Character dialogue gets memory driven by mental state
beats.summary: The newest paper criticizes mainstream conversational memory as passive and models shared history as part of an evolving relationship.

open_questions: Does dependency-aware state revision report the latency or token cost of propagating one changed fact through dependent memories?
Do the task-conditioned utility and exploration-task benchmarks report results for widely used vector-store or graph-based memory frameworks, or only research prototypes?
Does MIGRO show retrieval quality holding when the underlying model is swapped, and across which model families?
Does MemSeal publish a threat model or any evaluation of its provenance containment against memory-poisoning attempts?
Does mental-state-driven memory transfer from character dialogue to task-oriented agents?
